Exploratory data analysis: descriptive statistics of several variables

Source: R/eda_interactive.R
eda_describe.Rd

Computes descriptive statistics for several variables at once, optionally by group (e.g. a cluster solution) and weighted. Numeric variables are summarized by their mean, standard deviation, standard error, confidence interval and quantiles; categorical variables by their (weighted) frequency distribution, using the value labels.

Usage

eda_describe(
  data,
  vars,
  group = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  treat_as = c("auto", "numeric", "categorical"),
  conf_level = 0.95,
  total = FALSE,
  test = FALSE,
  test_method = c("parametric", "nonparametric"),
  reference = c("total", "rest", "meandev", "groups"),
  p_adjust = "holm",
  min_labels = 5
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, typically a haven-labelled tibble, or the output of seg_cluster() (see "Grouping by a cluster solution").

vars

The variables to describe: a character vector of names or a tidyselect expression, e.g. dplyr::starts_with("F50_0_").

group

Optional. Name of a grouping variable (e.g. "cluster_k4"). Respondents with a missing group are excluded.

weight

Optional. Name of a weight variable.

treat_as

"auto" (default), "numeric" or "categorical". See "Numeric or categorical?".

conf_level

Confidence level of the confidence intervals. Defaults to 0.95.

total

If TRUE and group is given, a "Total" group with all respondents is added. Defaults to FALSE.

test

If TRUE and group is given, group differences are tested with eda_test(). Defaults to FALSE.

test_method

"parametric" (default) or "nonparametric", passed to eda_test().

reference

Reference of the comparisons of the groups, passed to eda_test(): "total" (default, each group vs. the total including the group), "rest" (each group vs. the rest of the sample), "meandev" (each group vs. the mean of the group means) or "groups" (all pairs of groups). See eda_test(), "Statistical tests", for details.

p_adjust

Method to adjust the p-values of the comparisons (see stats::p.adjust()). Defaults to "holm".

min_labels

Minimum number of value labels or distinct values for a variable to be treated as numeric (with treat_as = "auto"). Defaults to 5.

Value

An object of class eda_describe, a list with the elements:

  • numeric: tibble with one row per numeric variable (and group): n (valid answers), n_eff (effective sample size, only if weighted), missing, mean, sd, se, ci_low, ci_high, median, q1, q3, min, max. NULL if there are no numeric variables.

  • categorical: tibble with one row per categorical variable, (group) and category: n (unweighted count), n_weighted and percent (weighted share among the valid answers, 0-100). NULL if there are no categorical variables.

  • tests: the eda_test() results if test = TRUE, otherwise NULL.

  • settings: list of the settings used.

Details

Numeric or categorical?

With treat_as = "auto", a variable is summarized as numeric (means) if it has at least min_labels value labels (e.g. a 5-point Likert scale), at least min_labels distinct observed values (e.g. a 1-10 scale with labelled end points only) or no value labels at all. Factors, character vectors and labelled variables with fewer values are summarized as categorical (frequency distributions). Use treat_as = "numeric" or "categorical" to treat all variables the same way.

Missing values

User-defined missing values (e.g. "don't know" = 99, kept by haven::read_sav(user_na = TRUE)) are set to NA before computing any statistic, so they never distort means or percentages.

Weights

If weight is given, means, standard deviations, quantiles and percentages are weighted. Standard errors and confidence intervals use the effective sample size of Kish, \(n_{eff} = (\sum w)^2 / \sum w^2\), which accounts for the loss of precision due to weighting (reported as n_eff).

Grouping by a cluster solution

data can also be the output of seg_cluster() (a seg_cluster or a seg_cluster_set). Its original data (data_full, all variables with labels, restricted to the clustered respondents) is used, and each cluster solution is added as a labelled grouping variable, e.g. cluster_k4 (noise points of density-based methods are labelled "Noise").

See also

eda_plot() to plot the statistics, eda_explore() to explore them interactively.

Other eda: eda_explore(), eda_plot(), eda_plot_detail(), eda_test()

Examples

# Means of a battery of rating items
eda_describe(sm_synthetic, vars = dplyr::starts_with("F50_0_"))

# By the benchmark segments, weighted, with tests of group differences
eda_describe(
  sm_synthetic,
  vars = c("F50_0_1", "F50_0_2", "gender"),
  group = "cluster_benchmark",
  weight = "weight",
  test = TRUE
)

# \donttest{
# By a cluster solution
prep <- seg_prep_data(sim_segments, vars = dplyr::starts_with("item_"), verbose = FALSE)
km <- seg_cluster(prep, k = 3, plots = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
eda_describe(km, vars = dplyr::starts_with("item_"), group = "cluster_k3")
